tools.name: get_pr
tools.description:
Return one pull request selected by its exact id from list_open_prs.

        The result includes the complete stored pull-request record. A title, URL,
        repository name, or unknown id is rejected rather than guessed.

tools.name: review_pr
tools.description:
Submit one review on an open pull request selected by exact pr_id.

        decision must be approve, request_changes, or comment. body may be omitted
        for approve. request_changes and comment require nonempty body text. The PR
        must already exist and be open. Returns the complete stored review record.

tools.name: list_open_prs
tools.description:
List identifying pull-request summaries. Defaults to open PRs.

        status may be open, closed, merged, or null for every status. repo and
        author filter by exact repository name and author key. assignee matches
        the assignees list; reviewer matches the reviewers list. These are separate
        relationships. Omitted filters do not restrict results. The summaries omit
        each pull request's body; use get_pr with an exact id to inspect the body.

tools.name: memanto_recall
tools.description: Search the Memanto memory agent by semantic similarity. Use this FIRST before asking the user to repeat information.

arguments.body: Request changes: deploy movement identity should use `(tenant_id, published_service_id, provenance_source, source_event_id)`. `ingestion_attempt_id` is delivery/audit metadata, not movement identity: retries may arrive under different attempts and still represent one movement, while rollback and redeploy are distinct movements even when service and transition/timing appear similar. The ten-minute `observed`-timestamp heuristic can merge real events and should not infer identity; when `source_event_id` is missing, render the movement unavailable rather than deduplicating heuristically. Please add regressions proving retries across different attempt IDs collapse, rollback and redeploy with distinct source-event IDs remain separate, and missing source-event IDs do not produce a guessed movement.

Requested changes on `lantern#1316`. The PR uses `ingestion_attempt_id` as identity and merges missing-source events by a ten-minute timestamp heuristic; both can misidentify movements. I asked for identity based on `(tenant_id, published_service_id, provenance_source, source_event_id)`, with missing source-event IDs shown as unavailable, and tests for retries, distinct rollback/redeploy events, and missing IDs.

pr.body: Changes deploy-movement identity to key records by tenant_id, published_service_id, provenance_source, and ingestion_attempt_id. When source_event_id is unavailable, records with the same service, transition, and a nearby observed timestamp are merged heuristically. Current tests cover repeated deliveries carrying the same ingestion-attempt ID, but do not include separate rollback and redeploy transitions.
pr.diff_summary: The movement key now uses ingestion_attempt_id in place of source_event_id. A ten-minute similarity window merges records lacking source_event_id when tenant, service, provenance, and transition match. Tests assert duplicate delivery suppression for a repeated attempt ID.
